source.title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics

accepted.question_text: Determine the physical origin and implications of the HERMES azimuthal asymmetry in semi-inclusive pion electroproduction from a longitudinally polarized proton target. In this setting, an observed pion azimuthal asymmetry could be a suppressed Collins-effect signal caused by the target spin's small component perpendicular to the virtual photon, or it could arise from twist-three helicity-flip effects suppressed by 1/Q. The open question is to distinguish these mechanisms and understand what the result implies for spin-dependent fragmentation measurements and access to transversity.

evidence.quote: What are the origins and implications of the Hermes azimuthal asymmetry?

This asymmetry could be a (suppressed) reflection of the Collins effect because the target spin, while parallel to the electron beam, has a small component, O(1/Q) perpendicular to the virtual photon. It could also result from competing twist-three helicity flip effects also suppressed by 1/Q.

accepted.question_text: Measure and determine the quark transversity distribution δq(x,Q²) in the nucleon. The leading-twist quark spin distributions in a nucleon include the unpolarized distribution q(x,Q²), the helicity distribution Δq(x,Q²), and the transversity distribution δq(x,Q²); δq governs helicity-flip or transverse-polarization physics and can be interpreted as the probability of finding quarks with momentum fraction x transversely polarized in a transversely polarized nucleon at infinite momentum. The open question is what δq(x,Q²) is experimentally and how to access it through processes such as transversely polarized Drell-Yan or semi-inclusive DIS with helicity-flip fragmentation.

evidence.quote: We now know that the transversity, δq(x, Q2), together with the unpolarized distribution, q(x, Q2), and the helicity distribution, Δq(x, Q2), are required to give a complete description of the quark spin in the nucleon at leading twist.
In contrast nothing is known about transversity from experiment, because it decouples from inclusive DIS on account of a selection rule.
Measurements of quark transversity rank high on the agendas of Hermes, COMPASS and RHIC.

accepted.question_text: Directly measure the polarized gluon distribution ΔG(x,Q²) in the nucleon and determine gross features of its shape. Indirect estimates can use the Q² dependence of the quark helicity distribution Δq(x,Q²) through renormalization group evolution, but the open question is to determine ΔG via direct probes such as photon-gluon fusion in charm, two-jet, or pion-pair production, or QCD Compton production of high-transverse-momentum photons or jets.

evidence.quote: A direct measurement of the polarized gluon distribution in the nucleon is probably the highest priority for QCD spin physics.
Further refinement of the indirect method will improve our knowledge of ΔG, but direct measurement is essential to determine gross features of its shape.
The basic mechanism is photon-gluon fusion.

accepted.question_text: Test whether the Gerasimov-Drell-Hearn-Hosada-Yamamoto sum rule is valid in QCD, or whether it can fail because the dispersion relation for the forward spin-flip Compton amplitude contains a nonzero constant term c0, historically called a J=1 fixed pole. The open question is whether J=1 fixed poles occur in QCD bound states; their presence could spoil the sum rule even when the relevant integral converges.
accepted.context_brief: DHGHY sum rule and J=1 fixed poles

evidence.quote: The question I would like to raise here is “What does the DHGHY Sum Rule test?”.
So the question of the validity of the DHGHY Sum Rule comes down to whether J = 1 fixed poles occur in QCD.
Still, the verdict is out in QCD, where bound states are not so simple.

accepted.question_text: Find a measurable and complete description of quark and gluon orbital angular momentum in the nucleon. A formal decomposition writes the nucleon's helicity as contributions from quark spin ΔΣ(x,Q²), gluon spin Δg(x,Q²), quark orbital angular momentum Lq(x,Q²), and gluon orbital angular momentum Lg(x,Q²), where Lq and Lg are Bjorken-x distributions in an infinite-momentum frame. The open question is how to measure Lq(x,Q²) or Lg(x,Q²), since they do not appear in the description of deeply virtual Compton scattering, and how to access experimentally the angular-momentum components that the theory defines.

evidence.quote: Most recently it has been possible to define gauge invariant parton distributions for all the components of the nucleon's angular momentum
On the other hand, eq. (5) suffers from a significant drawback: unlike Ji’s ˆLq, we know of no way to measure either Lq(x, Q2) or Lg(x, Q2). They do not appear in the description of DVCS.
Eq. 5 summarizes all we would like to know, but we do not know how to measure what we would like.

accepted.question_text: Determine the very-low-x behavior of the spin structure functions g1p(x,Q²) and g1n(x,Q²). Existing extrapolations suggested that both the proton and neutron g1 functions may become negative and diverge as x approaches 0; the open question is how this behavior is governed by the low-x, strong-coupling regime of QCD and what it implies for spin physics.

evidence.quote: What happens to g1(x, Q2) at very low x?

Reasonable extrapolations of existing data suggest that both g1p and g1n are negative and diverge as x → 0. This has little effect on the spin sum rules, but belongs to the new, interesting low-x, strong coupling regime of QCD.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether strange quarks s and anti-strange quarks s̄ in the nucleon have significantly different spatial and momentum distributions. C-even observables add s and s̄ contributions, while parity-violating electron scattering is sensitive to C-odd quantities such as strange magnetization and charge radius, and neutrino dimuon production can in principle separate s and s̄ momentum distributions. The open question is whether experiments can show significant s–s̄ differences.
accepted.context_brief: Strange and anti-strange quarks in the nucleon

evidence.quote: What are the properties of the s and s̄ quarks in the nucleon?
The next round of experiments should tell us whether s and s̄ quarks in the nucleon have significantly different spatial distributions.
Parity violating (xF3) dimuon production in neutrino DIS can, in principle, separate s and s̄ momentum distributions. Present data are not accurate enough to differentiate s and s̄.

accepted.question_text: Determine the size and significance of spin-dependent quark-gluon correlations in the nucleon, especially whether dynamical higher-twist contributions are always small. The open question is whether low-Q² lepton-scattering data can be connected to the deep-inelastic scattering regime by including only kinematic higher-twist effects, as in a generalized Wandzura-Wilczek approximation, thereby giving a theoretical foundation for parton-hadron duality speculations.

evidence.quote: What are the spin-dependent quark-gluon correlations in the nucleon?
The matrix elements of quark-gluon correlations can be extracted from these data. They appear very small. Perhaps dynamical higher twist is always small.
The generalized Wandzura-Wilczek approximation offers the promise of a solid theoretical foundations for speculations about “parton-hadron duality” in low energy lepton scattering.

accepted.question_text: Clarify the physical meaning of off-forward or skewed parton distributions measured in deeply virtual Compton scattering. Although these generalized distributions extend parton distribution functions away from the forward direction and can be measured with considerable effort, the open question is what they are heuristically and what hadron properties will be learned by measuring them.

evidence.quote: What can “off-forward” parton distributions tell us about hadron properties?
What is missing so far, to my taste, is a heuristic understanding of the physical significance of off-forward parton distributions.
We still need to figure out exactly what they are and what will we learn by measuring them.

accepted.question_text: Classify, relate, and interpret the expanding set of transverse-momentum-dependent and x-dependent distribution and fragmentation functions introduced for detailed DIS phenomena such as k⊥ distributions, higher twist, and semi-inclusive processes. The open questions are whether these functions are independent or connected by unrecognized symmetries, what physical interpretation fragmentation functions have analogous to the parton model for distributions, whether some functions are unnecessary, and how useful the Wandzura-Wilczek approximation is when it ignores dynamical higher twist.
accepted.context_brief: Proliferation of distribution and fragmentation functions

evidence.quote: Can some deeper order be found in the proliferation of k⊥ and x dependent distribution and fragmentation functions?

In response to new measurements of detailed properties in DIS (k⊥ distributions, higher twist, semi-inclusive processes), theorists have introduced a wonderful new zoo of distribution and fragmentation functions.

Now we need some clever zoology to classify, relate, and interpret these new functions. Are they all independent or are they related to one another by as yet unappreciated symmetries? What is the general physical interpretation of fragmentation functions analogous to the parton model of distribution functions? Perhaps some of them need to become extinct? How useful is the Wandzura-Wilczek approximation, which systematically ignores dynamical higher twist?

accepted.question_text: Improve the theoretical determination of higher-order QCD contributions to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment (g−2)μ. The open question is how to reduce the Standard Model uncertainty from QCD effects so that future higher-precision muon magnetic-moment measurements can more sharply test the Standard Model and possible extensions of it.

evidence.quote: At present the precision of the theoretical estimate of (gµ − 2) is principally limited by the lack of information on higher order QCD contributions, which require further study.
Approved experiments at BNL plan to reduce the statistical and systematic uncertainties on aµ to about 0.3 ppm, making better understanding of the QCD contribution a very high priority.

accepted.question_text: Search for CP violation beyond the CKM mechanism through electric dipole moments, especially the muon electric dipole moment. Since Standard Model CKM predictions for EDMs are far below experimental goals, the open question is whether new sources of CP violation can produce a measurable EDM, potentially at sensitivities comparable to existing constraints on the anomalous magnetic moment.
accepted.context_brief: Muon EDM and new CP violation

evidence.quote: If all CP-violation is encoded in the CKM matrix, EDMs are too small to measure. Therefore EDMs are an excellent place to look for CP-violation beyond the Standard Model.
Attempts to explain the origin of the baryon excess in the Universe suggest that other sources of CP-violation may be waiting to be discovered.
So EDM measurements at a sensitivity comparable to existing limits on aµ could provide fertile ground in which to look for new sources of CP-violation.
